Renewables

Land baselines and construction evidence for renewable projects

What was on your site before you arrived, what stands on and around it and along the connection line, and how construction has progressed between visits. Dated, reviewed by a person and delivered as files your development, E&S and construction teams can use.

Send us your site boundary and connection route How the method works

The problem, in your words

The land question arrives before the first panel

Utility-scale solar and wind projects are land projects first. Lenders and their technical advisers want a clean land history, the connection line needs a servitude across other people’s land, the ESIA needs a land-cover baseline, and construction has to be evidenced against the programme. Each of those questions is easier to answer from dated imagery than from a site visit.

“What was on this land before we arrived?”

Development and permitting teams need a dated land history for the site and the connection route, for due diligence and the ESIA.

“The connection line crosses dozens of properties.”

Grid constraints push projects to build their own connection lines, and each one needs a servitude and a count of what it would affect.

“We need construction evidence for the lenders.”

Owners’ engineers and lenders’ technical advisers need dated evidence of earthworks and progress between site visits.

Who this is for

  • IPP development managers
  • Land and permitting leads
  • Environmental assessment practitioners
  • EPC construction managers
  • Owners’ engineers and lenders’ technical advisers

Site selection and due diligence

A dated land history for each candidate site

For each candidate site and connection route, the imagery history shows what has been built, cleared or cultivated, and roughly when, from archived satellite imagery and open datasets. A land-use and land-cover baseline maps built-up land, cropland, bare ground, water and tree cover, combined with our structure register, for the ESIA. Terrain and flood screening highlights steep, erosion-prone and historically flooded ground.

We then compare the options side by side: structures affected, land cover and screening results for each site and each connection route. It is an input to your site selection, not a full alternatives assessment, and the land history is not a title, tenure or valuation check.

What you receive

  • An imagery history for each candidate site and route
  • A land-use and land-cover baseline for the ESIA
  • A site and connection-route comparison table
  • Slope, erosion and flood-exposure screening

Structures on the site and along the connection line

What the site and its line would affect

We map the structures inside the site boundary and in a ring around it, and along the connection line within the servitude width and any wider band you choose, each measured to the boundary or the line. Where structures or land uses are affected, a dated register of the structures in the footprint, with reviewer categories, supports your census and asset inventory under IFC Performance Standard 5. It supports the census; it does not replace it.

Encroachment surveys

Structures inside a concession, site or boundary, in a ring around it, or both, mapped and listed so you can see where land is being occupied.

Construction and earthworks

Dated progress between site visits

Dated drone orthophotos and elevation models of the site, compared side by side, show where ground has been cut or filled between visits, and volumes of stockpiles and spoil are calculated from the elevation models. Heavy plant and equipment visible on each survey date is recorded as a snapshot of activity on site. Drone surveys are subject to the permits and authorisations each job requires.

These records give owners’ engineers and lenders’ advisers dated evidence to set against the construction programme. They are not certified surveys or a quantity surveyor’s valuation, and we make no promise of turnaround for bid windows before the scope is agreed.

What you receive

  • Side-by-side dated orthophotos and elevation models
  • Cut-and-fill maps between visits
  • Stockpile and spoil volumes
  • Plant and equipment visible on each survey date

Drone surveys

Orthophotos, elevation models and volumes where the detail matters, subject to the permits and authorisations each job requires.

Fire near the site

Fire-hotspot notices and burnt-area maps

In the dry season, grass fires threaten site boundaries, substations and connection lines. Fire hotspots detected by satellite near your site and line are filtered to the buffer around them, checked by a reviewer and sent as notices, followed by maps of the burnt area. The hotspot data comes from NASA FIRMS. This is not an emergency or early-warning service, and small, short-lived or cloud-covered fires can be missed.

Mozambique, South Africa, Nigeria

Where renewable projects meet land rules

A summary for orientation, as of 26 September 2026, not legal advice.

English

South Africa

Grid constraints mean many projects, from public procurement rounds to private wheeling deals, build their own connection lines, and each needs a servitude and a count of the structures it would affect. Lenders apply the Equator Principles and the IFC Performance Standards. Commercial drone work needs a UASOC and an Air Service Licence under Civil Aviation Regulations Part 101.

Português · English

Mozambique

In Mozambique the larger land question for new generation is resettlement on hydropower and associated line projects, covered on our project finance and ESIA page. Connection lines fall under the servitude rules of the Electricity Law, described on the power and utilities page.

English

Nigeria

Solar-hybrid mini-grids are the main renewable build-out, and their land questions are household estimates and site histories for candidate communities, covered under mini-grid and electrification planning.

Honest scope

What we do, and what we don’t

What we do

  • Map land history, land cover and structures on and around sites and lines
  • Compare candidate sites and connection routes by the land they affect
  • Record dated construction progress, volumes and plant on site
  • Filter satellite fire hotspots to your buffers and map burnt areas

What we don’t do

  • Inspect panels, turbines, substations or other equipment
  • Assess solar or wind resource, or grid capacity
  • Verify title or tenure, or value land
  • Issue statutory surveys or quantity valuations

Frequently asked questions

Can you help us choose between candidate sites?

Yes. For each candidate site and connection route we compare the structures affected, the land cover, the imagery history and the terrain and flood screening, as an input to your own site selection.

Do we need a resettlement baseline for a solar or wind project?

Only where structures or land uses are affected. If they are, a dated register of the structures in the footprint and along the connection line supports your census and asset inventory under IFC Performance Standard 5, where lenders apply it.

Are your construction volumes a quantity survey?

No. Cut-and-fill maps and volumes from drone elevation models give dated evidence of progress. They are not a certified survey or a quantity surveyor’s valuation.

Can you inspect our panels or turbines?

No. We map land, structures and earthworks around your site. Equipment inspection is outside our services.

Send us your site boundary and connection route

Tell us the stage of the project, from site selection to construction, and we reply with a scope, an imagery plan and a written proposal.
